summary: @servicetitan/confirm-navigation ships preinstall alternate-runtime dropper executing obfuscated Bun payload
details: package.json declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs is obfuscated (obfuscator.io _0xNNNN identifiers) and, at npm install time, detects the host platform and libc variant, downloads a pinned Bun runtime zip from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts the bun binary to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it to run the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 711 KB single-line Bun-compiled bundle (// @bun @bun-cjs header) using string-array rotation (WV8StW) and character-mapping decoder tables, unrelated to any React confirm-navigation UI code. The alternate Bun runtime is fetched specifically to execute this opaque bundled payload — a legitimate React navigation-confirmation helper has no need for a separate language runtime at install. The package publishes under the @servicetitan npm scope with homepage docs.st.dev and repo servicetitan/anvil-uikit-contrib, yet the shipped contents (obfuscated preinstall launcher + ~700 KB Bun payload) do not match the advertised confirm-navigation utility, causing installers who trust the @servicetitan namespace to execute arbitrary author-controlled code on npm install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
